# Progress 2026

> Progress 2026 (https://progress.dealwithmuhammad.com) is a free web app that shows, live, how much of the year 2026 has passed in the visitor's own time zone: a percentage updated every second, a progress bar, the days elapsed and the days left until 2027. It was designed and built by Muhammad Ahmad, a web and mobile app developer in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

No sign-up, no ads, free to use. The page also shows a server-rendered summary and FAQ (refreshed hourly and labelled with the current UTC date) for readers and crawlers that don't run JavaScript.

## What it shows

- The percentage of 2026 that has passed, updated every second
- Any other year or range of years from 1900 to 2100 (for example 2027, 2026–2030 or 2010–2027), chosen with quick buttons (This year, Next year, Next 5 years, This decade, Last 10 years) or From/To menus. Future ranges show 0% and the days until they start; past ranges show 100%. Shareable links: ?year=2027 or ?from=2026&to=2030
- A progress bar, with a line where each new year begins in a multi-year range
- Days elapsed (full days completed since 1 January) and days remaining (counting today)
- The visitor's location, flag, local date and time
- A Location menu to switch to any city or IANA time zone
- Light and dark themes

## How the percentage is calculated

- Percentage = (time since 00:00 on 1 January 2026, in the selected time zone) ÷ (length of 2026) × 100
- 2026 is not a leap year, so the year is 365 days long (8,760 hours, 31,536,000 seconds); a leap year would use 366 days
- It uses wall-clock time in the selected time zone, so at the same moment visitors in different time zones can see slightly different values
- The time zone is detected automatically from the visitor's IP address, falling back to the browser's time zone, and can be changed by hand
- Before 2026 begins the counter shows 0%; after 31 December 2026 it shows 100%
- One day is about 0.274% of the year; one hour is about 0.0114%

## Facts about 2026

- 365 days; not a leap year (the next leap year is 2028)
- Starts on Thursday 1 January 2026 and ends on Thursday 31 December 2026
- 52 weeks and 1 day; 53 weeks in the ISO 8601 week-numbering system, because it starts on a Thursday
- 1 January 2027 is a Friday
